name: Flat-fee exit marketplace for sub-$10K directories and micro-sites
buyer: Owners of small sites or directories selling a roughly $1K-$10K asset, plus indie buyers
pain: Stacked fees (listing, commission, add-ons) take a meaningful chunk of small sales, and tiny assets have a thin buyer pool.
wedge: A niche-directory-only exit marketplace with a flat or very low fee, using a third-party escrow provider rather than holding funds.

scan1Edge.entrant_basis: A flat 5% fee on a $5K sale gives $250. The incumbent figure is derived as 10% of $5,000 plus the $29 listing fee (C10, C11). Vertos and ExitBid already claim comparable prices.
scan1Edge.falsifier: If sellers can already list at roughly $0-$250 on Vertos or ExitBid, the price advantage over those rivals is zero. Price alone is not a defensible edge.
scan1Edge.unit: USD seller cost on a $5,000 sale

substitutesNoted.name: Flippa
substitutesNoted.price_point: 10% commission plus listing from $29; ~$529 on a $5K sale

substitutesNoted.name: Vertos
substitutesNoted.price_point: Free listing, flat 5% on sale (vendor claim)

unitEconomicsNoted.notes: ESTIMATE: 5% of a $5K deal gives $250; the margin is from the notes. Volume would be very low and escrow provider fees are not included.

majorUncertainty: Whether any buyer pool for sub-$10K directories can be assembled when several cheaper or free rivals already exist.
unknowns: Whether Acquire.com sellers pay or list free (sources disagree)
Actual deal volume of Vertos and ExitBid
Whether buyers are reachable in a niche-directory segment
The Hacker News 'Show HN: Acquire Directory' signal (2 points, 0 comments) is not in the excerpt lists, so it is not cited
regulatoryOrPlatformDependency: Escrow and payment handling raises money-transmission risk, so it would need to use an existing escrow provider. Buyer-side fraud and fake revenue claims need handling.
